name: system.power.sleep
description: Suspend the machine to sleep (S3 — RAM stays powered, disks spin down). With `delay_seconds: 0`, the connection may drop before any response. With `delay_seconds > 0`, the OK with `scheduled_at` arrives before sleep is issued.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before initiating sleep. Zero means immediate.

wake_at.description: Unix epoch (seconds) to wake the machine. The agent uses a Win32 waitable timer to schedule the wake. Returns `ERR not_supported {"reason":"vm_environment"}` when `system.info.capabilities.wake_timer_supported` is false; pass `bypass_vm_check: true` to bypass the gate.

bypass_vm_check.description: Bypass the VM-environment check for `wake_at`. No effect when `wake_at` is not specified.

reason.description: Free-form reason logged with the sleep event. Surfaced in Windows Event Log on platforms that record it.

scheduled_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when sleep will fire. Equals now+delay_seconds. Only present when delay_seconds > 0.

x-implementations.name: set_suspend_state
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SetSuspendState(Hibernate=FALSE, ForceCritical=FALSE, DisableWakeEvent=FALSE)`. Available NT 5+ (Win 2000 onwards). When `wake_at` is supplied, the agent first arms a `SetWaitableTimerEx` wake timer.

windows-modern.description: SetSuspendState with Hibernate=FALSE. Returns ERR not_supported when sleep is disabled at the BIOS/firmware level or when hardware lacks S3 support. VM guests typically report `system.info.capabilities.wake_timer_supported: false`; `wake_at` requests on such guests return ERR not_supported {"reason":"vm_environment"} unless `bypass_vm_check: true`. Hyper-V on Win 11 hosts is the most reliable VM target; older hypervisors may return success without de-allocating the guest.

windows-classic.description: SetSuspendState with Hibernate=FALSE. Available NT 5+ (Win 2000, XP, Vista, 7, 8, 8.1). NT 4 returns ERR not_supported (no power management subsystem). `wake_at` with `SetWaitableTimerEx` is available NT 5.1+ (XP); NT 4 / 2000 reject `wake_at` regardless of `bypass_vm_check`.
